questions.question: In which year was Battle of Peshawar fought between Raja Jayapal and Mahmud Ghazni?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Battle of Peshawar between Raja Jayapala **and **Mahmud of Ghazni **took place in the year **1001 CE.**
 
• **Raja Jayapala **was the ruler of the **Hindu Shahi dynasty** in the region, while **Mahmud of Ghazni** was a prominent **Muslim conqueror** from the Ghaznavid dynasty.
 
• The battle resulted in the defeat of **Raja Jayapala** and marked the beginning of **Mahmud's invasions** into the **Indian subcontinent.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Hindu Shahi dynasty** was a** medieval Indian dynasty** that ruled the region of **Gandhara (present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan)** from the **9th to the 10th centuries CE.**
 
• They were known as the** "Shahi" **or** "Kings of the Shahis"** and were primarily of **Hindu faith,** although some rulers may have embraced **Buddhism **as well.
 
• The dynasty's origins are believed to be in the **ancient Gandhara region,** which had a rich history and was a center of Buddhist culture.
 
• The Hindu Shahis emerged as a powerful dynasty in the wake of the decline of the** Turk Shahi dynasty.**
 
• **The Hindu Shahi rulers** were known for their resistance against the **Arab and Turkic invasions** from the west.
 
• They successfully defended their territories against several attempts at conquest by Muslim armies, including the expeditions of Arab general Qutayba ibn Muslim in the 8th century.

questions.question: Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled 14 feet high statue of Lok Nayak Jayprakash Narayan in ______ in October 2022.

• **Union Home Minister Amit Shah **unveiled a 14 feet high statue of** Lok Nayak Jayprakash Narayan in Sitabdiara**, **Saran district,** **Bihar** in **October 2022**​.
 
• **Political Activist and Leader:**
 
 
• **​**Lok Nayak Jayprakash Narayan, often referred to as JP, was a prominent Indian political leader and activist.
 
• He played a significant role in the Indian independence movement and was a staunch advocate for social and political reform in post-independence India.
 
 
 
• **Total Revolution Movement:**
 
 
• **​**JP is best remembered for leading the "Total Revolution" movement in the 1970s.
 
• This was a public campaign against corruption and the increasing authoritarianism of the Indian government at the time, especially during the period of the Emergency declared by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
 
 
• **Sampoorna Kranti (Total Revolution):**
 
 
• **​**JP's concept of "Sampoorna Kranti" or "Total Revolution" encompassed various aspects of society, including social, political, economic, and cultural transformations.
 
• He called for a complete overhaul of the system to achieve a truly democratic society.
 
 
 
• **Bihar Movement:**
 
 
• **Jayprakash Narayan** led the **Bihar Movement in the mid-1970s**, a popular uprising in the Indian state of Bihar that aimed to bring about greater accountability and transparency in the government.
 
 
 
• **Awards and Honors:**
 
 
• **​**JP was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1999 for his significant contributions to Indian society and politics.
 
• He remains a respected figure in Indian history, and his life and works continue to inspire political activism and social reform in the country.

questions.question: The monetary policy instrument called ‘bank rate’ is aligned to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marginal standing facility rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Marginal standing facility rate**

 
 
• It is the rate at which banks borrow funds overnight from the RBI against approved government securities.
 
• Under MSF, banks can borrow funds up to one percentage of their net demand and time liabilities (NDTL).
 
• It used by banks to borrow from the Reserve Bank of India in an emergency situation when inter-bank liquidity dries up completely.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Liquidity adjustment facility**

 
 
• The RBI introduced the LAF as a result of the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee on Banking Sector Reforms (1998). 
 
• A liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) is a tool used in monetary policy, primarily by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI),
 
• It allows banks to borrow money through repurchase agreements (repos) or for banks to make loans to the RBI through reverse repo agreements.
 
• This arrangement manages liquidity pressures and assures basic stability in the financial markets.
 
 
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio 
 
 
• Commercial banks have to hold a certain minimum amount of deposit as reserves with the central bank
 
• The percentage of cash required to be kept in reserves as against the bank's total deposits is called the Cash Reserve Ratio
 
• The cash reserve is either stored in the bank’s vault or is sent to the RBI
 
• Banks can’t lend the CRR money to corporates or individual borrowers, banks can’t use that money for investment purposes.

questions.question: What are hardware devices that retrieve data from a computer system and further translate the received data into a form understandable to humans?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **__Output Devices__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

 
• **Hardware devices** that **retrieve data** from a **computer system** and translate the received data into a form understandable to humans are known as **output devices.**
 
• These devices take **digital information from a computer **and convert it into a **human-readable format.**

Some common examples of output devices include:

 
• **Monitor/Display:** A visual output device that presents information in the** form of text, images, and graphics on a screen.**
 
• **Printer: **Prints digital data onto physical paper in the form **of text, images, or both.**
 
• **Speaker:** Converts digital audio data into an **audible sound, allowing users to hear sounds, music, or other audio output.**
 
• **Projector: **Displays computer-generated images or video onto a larger screen or projection surface, often used for presentations or home theater setups.
 
• **Headphones/Earphones: **Output devices that provide audio output directly to the user's ears, allowing for private listening.
 
• **Plotter:** A device used to produce high-quality, large-scale graphics or drawings based on computer instructions.

questions.question: Who of the following person wrote a book named Kitab-ul-Hind?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Al-Biruni.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__****The Kitab-ul-Hind:**

 
• Al-Biruni’s Kitab-ul-Hind, written in Arabic, is simple and lucid.
 
• It is a voluminous text, divided into 80 chapters on subjects such as religion and philosophy, festivals, astronomy, alchemy, manners and customs, social life, weights and measures, iconography, laws, and metrology.
 
• Generally (though not always), Al-Biruni adopted a distinctive structure in each chapter, beginning with a question, following this up with a description based on Sanskritic traditions, and concluding with a comparison with other cultures.
 
• Some present-day scholars have argued that this almost geometric structure, remarkable for its precision and predictability, owed much to his mathematical orientation.
 
• Al-Biruni, who wrote in Arabic, probably intended his work for peoples living along the frontiers of the subcontinent.
 
• He was familiar with translations and adaptations of Sanskrit, Pali, and Prakrit texts into Arabic – these ranged from fables to works on astronomy and medicine. However, he was also critical of the ways in which these texts were written and clearly wanted to improve on them.

questions.question: Which amendment in the Indian constitution is related to extension of jurisdiction of High Courts to Union territories?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer is __**7th Amendment**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****7th Constitutional amendment act(1956):**

__
 
• Abolishing the previous classification of state into four categories.
 
• Extended the jurisdiction of high courts to union territories.__
 
• Provided for the establishment of a **common court for 2 or more states.**
 
• Provided for the appointment of additional acting judges of the high court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****1st Constitutional amendment act(1951):**

 
• It was crucial in facilitating **land reforms in India.**
 
• Added Article 31A and Article 31B to protect laws related to the acquisition of estates and other land reforms from judicial scrutiny.
 
• Empowered the state to make special provisions for the advancement of **socially and economically backward class.**
 
• Provided for the saving of laws providing for the acquisition of estate, etc.
 
• Added the** ninth schedule** to protect the land reform and other laws included in the form of the judicial review.
 
• Added three more grounds of restriction on freedom of speech and expression viz, public order, friendly relation with foreign states, and incitement to an offense. It also made the** restriction reasonable and thus justiciable.**
 
• Provided that the state trading and nationalization of any trade or business by any state is not to be invalid on the ground of violation of the right to trade or business.

**13th Constitutional amendment act(1962):**

 
• Gave the status of state to Nagaland and made a special provision for it.

9th Constitutional amendment act(1960):

 
• It primarily dealt with the re-adjustment of the boundaries between India and Pakistan.
 
• Facilitate the cession of the Berubari union.

questions.question:
The simultaneous shifts of both the demand curve and the supply curve can happen in which of the following ways?

I. Supply curve shifts leftward and demand curve shifts rightward.

II. Both supply and demand curves shift leftwards.

III. Supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The supply curve shifts leftward and demand curve shifts rightward.**

 
 
• This combination of shifts will lead to an increase in the **equilibrium price and a decrease in the equilibrium quantity.**
 
• For example,** if there is a natural disaster that** **destroys a large portion of the cropland, then the supply curve for food will shift leftward.**
 
• **At the same time, if people's incomes increase, then the demand curve for food will shift rightward.**
 
• The net effect of these two shifts will be** an increase in the price of food and a decrease in the quantity of food that is consumed.**
 
 

***Hence statement I is correct.***

 
• **Both supply and demand curves shift leftwards.**

 
 
• This combination of shifts will lead to a decrease in the equilibrium price and a decrease in the equilibrium quantity.
 
• For example, **if there is a strike by workers in the auto industry, then the supply curve for cars will shift leftward.**
 
• **At the same time, if people's incomes decrease, then the demand curve for cars will shift leftward.**
 
• The net effect of these two shifts will be a decrease in the price of cars and a decrease in the quantity of cars that are sold.
 
 

*Hence statement II is correct.*

 
• **Supply curve shifts rightward and demand curve shifts leftward.**

 
 
• This combination of shifts will lead to an ambiguous change in the equilibrium price and a decrease in the equilibrium quantity.
 
• For example, **if there is a technological breakthrough that makes it cheaper to produce cars, then the supply curve for cars will shift rightward.**
 
• At the same time, if people's incomes decrease, then the demand curve for cars will shift leftward.
 
• The net effect of these two shifts **will be a decrease in the equilibrium quantity of cars, but the direction of the change in the equilibrium price is ambiguous.**
 
 

*Hence statement III is correct.*

questions.question: The Earth has been divided into many time zones. How many degrees does each time zone covers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 degrees**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Each time zone covers 15 degrees of longitude.**
 
• There are 24 time zones in the world, so the Earth is divided into **360/24 = 15 degrees of longitude per time zone.**
 
 
• **24 degrees is the total number of degrees in a circle.**
 
• **20 degrees is not a common number of degrees for a time zone,.**
 
• **10 degrees is to Indian Standard Time o small to be a useful division of the Earth.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• India uses a** single time zone, Indian Standard Time (IST), which is UTC+5:30.**
 
• This means that IST is **5 and a half hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a5cbce71d0e4d1726e061cd2ede0925e355cb9ed59f55f449c338f43e1dfe14.png]
